experiences.title: PMA 152 • Karachi centre
experiences.summary: Only 4 out of 25 candidates were selected that day. The officer asked the meaning of his name, asked him to introduce himself, and asked why his grades were so low. He honestly said it was his own fault because he gave more time to sports, and he did not blame his school or college. The officer then asked quick estimation questions and talked about his sports for 3-4 minutes. He believes neat dress, eye contact, a smile and fluent English got him easy questions while others got hard geography questions.
asked: What is the meaning of your name?
Please introduce yourself.
Your grades are very low. Why?
If I ask you to go and touch the Arabian Sea and come back, how much time will it take?
What is the length and width of the table in front of me? Show me.
Which sports do you play? (detailed questions on sports)
tips: If your marks are low, accept it honestly; do not blame your school, college or anyone else.
Keep eye contact and a natural smile throughout the interview.
Wear a light-coloured full-sleeve formal shirt (sleeves not folded), dark dress pants and formal lace-up shoes; no jeans or loafers.
Be ready for practical estimation questions like distance, time or the size of an object.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Quetta centre
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on 'A wealthy life is better than a peaceful life' and an Urdu essay on the role of teacher, student and parents in education. A Lieutenant Colonel and a Major asked about his district, his college and why he wants to join the Army. When asked about the Indus civilization, he honestly said he is weak in Pakistan Studies and asked for science questions, and the panel agreed. The Major also asked why he did not go for MDCAT, about his time as house prefect, and what big thing he wants to do for his family, province and country.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your district.
Tell me about your college.
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
What is the Indus civilization?
What are algae, fungi, chromosomes, ions and ionic bonds?
What is Newton's second law and its equation?
Your favourite subject is biology, so why did you not appear in the MDCAT?
You were a house prefect. Tell me about leadership at your level.
What big thing do you want to do for your family, your province and the people of Pakistan?
tips: If you are weak in one area, say so honestly and offer your strong subject; the panel may accept it.
Be ready to explain any leadership role (like prefect) written in your form.
Prepare a clear answer for why you chose the Army over other careers.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Rawalpindi centre
experiences.summary: He wrote an English and an Urdu essay before the interview. The board was a Lieutenant Colonel and a female psychologist Major. He knocked, asked permission, greeted, sat straight and kept eye contact. The Colonel asked about his area, his father's job, his old schools and boarding-school life, then told him to speak for 2 minutes on hostel life, followed by a few quick GK questions. The psychologist asked nothing.
asked: Which area are you from?
What does your father do and where is he posted?
Tell us about your previous schools and colleges.
Speak for 2 minutes on the impact of hostel life.
What is the full form of OGRA?
What is the currency of Bangladesh?
What is the currency of Iran?
What is the currency of Gilgit-Baltistan? (trick question)
Who is the Governor of Punjab?
What is 5% of 500?
tips: Knock, ask permission, greet with Assalam-o-Alaikum and sit only when told.
Sit straight, do not cross your legs or lock your hands, and look the interviewer in the eye.
Confidence and body language matter more than the number of right answers.
Learn currencies, capitals, and the names of the President, PM, Chief Ministers and Governors.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Faisalabad centre
experiences.summary: A Lieutenant Colonel and a Captain took the interview. After his introduction, the Lt Col asked about his father, siblings, three strengths, three weaknesses and his plan B. Because he said he had no interest in football, he was tested on current sports news like the FIFA World Cup and a cricket series in Pakistan. The Captain then asked questions from his bio data form. He was nervous at first, but the panel made him comfortable.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your father.
Do you have any siblings? What are their names and what do they do?
Tell me three strengths of yours.
Tell me three weaknesses of yours.
What is your plan B?
Are you interested in football? Where is the FIFA World Cup being held?
What is the capital of that country?
Which teams reached the World Cup semi-final?
Which foreign cricket team is touring Pakistan now, and what was the last match result?
Questions from your bio data form
tips: Follow current news, including big sports events, even if they are not your hobby.
Prepare three strengths and three weaknesses in advance.
Nervousness usually goes away after the first few questions, so keep going calmly.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Multan centre
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on unemployment and an Urdu essay on the qualities of a good student. He asked permission to enter, stood beside the chair and sat only when told. The Colonel asked him to introduce himself, then asked biology questions and questions on Pakistan's constitutions. The psychologist asked what he would do if not recommended and who Edhi was. He left politely with a smile.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What are the longest and smallest bones of the human body?
What are the types of blood cells?
What is the difference between a plant cell and an animal cell?
Who was the first President of Pakistan?
How many constitutions has Pakistan had?
What is the difference between the 1962 and 1973 constitutions?
If we do not recommend you, what will you do?
Who was Abdul Sattar Edhi?
tips: Ask 'May I come in, sir?', stand beside the chair and sit only when told.
Revise the basics of your FSc subjects, because the Colonel may ask from them.
End with a polite thank you and salam.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Peshawar centre (Hafiz, economics student)
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on whether college students should choose their own subjects and an Urdu essay on new technology making people lazy. The Colonel asked how many times he had applied and why he changed his centre. He could not explain the difference between a credit and a debit card even though he studies economics, and kept saying sorry. Because he wrote that he is a Hafiz, the psychologist asked Islamic questions, including the meaning of a Quran word, which he could not answer. He was not recommended.
asked: What are you doing these days?
How many times have you applied for army tests?
Why did you change your test centre?
What is the difference between a credit card and a debit card?
What do you know about fighter pilots?
What do you think about travelling by train?
What is democracy?
Are you a Hafiz-e-Quran?
What is the meaning of 'Wal-yatalattaf', the middle word of the Quran?
What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
After how many years did Hazrat Yusuf (AS) meet his father?
tips: Know the basics of your own subject; failing an easy question from your own field hurts a lot.
If you write that you are a Hafiz, expect Quran questions and learn the meaning of what you memorised.
Saying 'sorry' again and again gives a bad impression; prepare well.
Have a clear reason ready if you changed your centre or applied many times.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • South Waziristan candidate
experiences.summary: He wrote 'Knowledge is power' in English and the importance of religion in human life in Urdu. A Colonel asked where he is from, where he lives now, and about his education and siblings. A Major then asked general knowledge questions, and he politely said sorry for one he did not know. At the end the Colonel asked how he thought his interview went and wished him luck.
asked: Where are you from, and where are you settled now?
Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your education.
Tell me about your siblings.
Who was the first President of the USA?
What is the capital of Australia?
Which metal is found in liquid form at room temperature?
Name the rivers of KPK.
What is GPS?
What are the official and national languages of Pakistan and India?
How do you think your interview went?
tips: Ask permission before sitting down and keep eye contact.
GK alone does not decide the result; show confidence but do not be overconfident.
If you do not know an answer, politely say sorry.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Rawalpindi centre (GK and Islamic history)
experiences.summary: After the introduction, the interviewer asked mostly general knowledge and Islamic history questions. He was asked about Indian cities, US states, Pakistan-India wars and NATO. He could not answer some questions, like the main enemy in Ghazwa-e-Khandaq, but he still passed. He was also asked whether any relative serves in the Army.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Name 5 cities of India.
Name 5 states of the USA.
How many wars have been fought between Pakistan and India, and when?
What is NATO?
Who are the Azwaj-e-Mutahharat (wives of the Holy Prophet PBUH)?
Who is called Saifullah?
In which Hijri year was Ghazwa-e-Khandaq fought, and who was the main enemy?
Do you have any relative serving in the Army?
tips: You can pass even if you cannot answer every GK question.
Revise Pakistan-India wars, NATO and the main battles of Islamic history.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Peshawar centre (second attempt)
experiences.summary: He was not recommended in the PMA 150 initial interview and tried again. He wrote an English essay on the role of parents in raising children and an Urdu essay on hard work and good luck. The Lieutenant Colonel asked where Russia is and why he was not recommended last time. The Major asked about current office holders and asked him to show Russia on a map. He took a moment to think, answered calmly, and passed.
asked: What is your name?
Where is Russia?
Why were you not recommended in your last initial interview?
Who is the Chairman Senate?
Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly?
Who was the previous President of Pakistan, and where is he now?
Do you know how to read a map? Show Russia on the map.
tips: If you failed before, explain honestly why and what you have improved.
Practise finding countries on a world map.
Know current office holders like the Chairman Senate, NA Speaker and the previous President.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Swat area candidate
experiences.summary: A Colonel took the interview. He asked what the candidate is doing these days and why he chose the Army when there are thousands of other jobs. He asked about the current situation in Swat and how militants get food and shelter. Then he switched the interview to English and asked basic grammar questions. He also asked why the candidate did not choose medicine after good FSc pre-medical marks, and why he wrote video games as a hobby.
asked: How do you pronounce your name?
What are you doing these days?
Why did you choose the Pak Army when there are thousands of other jobs?
What is the situation in Swat right now?
From where do the Taliban get their food, shelter and water?
What is the national language of Pakistan?
What is the official language of Pakistan?
What is the currency of Afghanistan?
What is active voice and passive voice?
What is a noun and what is a verb?
You got good marks in FSc pre-medical, so why did you not choose medicine?
Why did you write playing video games as your hobby?
tips: Know the latest news about your own home area.
Be ready for the officer to switch from Urdu to English.
Be ready to explain every hobby you write in your form.
If you do not know an answer, simply say 'Sorry sir, I don't know'.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Karachi centre
experiences.summary: He knocked, asked permission, and stood by the chair until told to sit. The board was a Colonel and a psychologist Major. After his introduction he was asked about the Indus Waters Treaty, which he explained in detail, and about the 1973 constitution. He was also asked about his strengths and weaknesses. The interview took about 9 minutes.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What is the Indus Waters Treaty?
Tell us about the constitution of Pakistan.
What is the 1973 constitution?
What are your strengths and weaknesses?
tips: Stand by the chair and sit only when asked.
Prepare an honest list of your strengths and weaknesses.
Prepare national topics like the Indus Waters Treaty and the 1973 constitution.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Rawalpindi centre (speech)
experiences.summary: He had to give a speech on why Pakistan's education system is declining. The psychologist asked him about 10 GK questions and he could answer only 4 or 5, saying sorry for the rest. The two written essays carried 20 marks (10 English, 10 Urdu) and he did them well. He believes his good essays and confident speech got him recommended even though his GK was weak.
asked: Give a speech on the reasons behind the decline of the education system in Pakistan.
What is the currency of Turkey?
Where is the White Sea?
Where is the Yellow Sea?
Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan?
What is 5% of 700?
What was the old name of Makkah?
tips: The written essays carry about 20 marks (10 English, 10 Urdu), so practise both.
A good speech and good essays can make up for weak GK answers.
Keep current affairs updated, like the names of Chief Ministers.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Rawalpindi centre (psychologist first)
experiences.summary: He wrote an Urdu essay on the importance of law in society and an English essay on 'Money or Wisdom'. At first only the lady psychologist was in the room, and later a Colonel came in. She asked him to introduce himself, why he wants to join the Army, and some GK questions. He politely said 'Sorry madam' for the ones he did not know. At the end he spoke for 2 minutes on 'Armed Forces'.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Who is the President of Russia?
What is the full form of FATA?
What was the old name of Faisalabad?
Speak for 2 minutes on the topic 'Armed Forces'.
tips: Take permission before entering and before sitting.
They mainly check your confidence and the way you talk.
If you do not know an answer, say sorry politely instead of guessing.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Lt Col and Major board
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on co-education and an Urdu essay on local tourism. The Lieutenant Colonel asked about his qualification, father's job and family, and even personal and honesty questions. The Major asked about his hobbies and brothers, and then he was asked why he wants to join the Army. He could not answer five GK questions, so the Lt Col told him to improve his GK.
asked: What is your qualification?
Tell me about your father and family.
Do you have a girlfriend?
What are your hobbies?
Tell me about your brothers.
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Have you ever watched restricted websites?
Do you tell lies?
Five general knowledge questions
tips: Answer personal and honesty questions truthfully and calmly.
Prepare general knowledge well, because weak GK is noticed.
Leave properly: stand up, thank them, say salam and walk out calmly.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Cricket player
experiences.summary: The interview was mostly a talk based on his interview form. After a short introduction he was asked about the Suez and Panama canals. Because he wrote cricket as his hobby, there was a long discussion on cricket records and the best team.
asked: Introduce yourself briefly.
Tell me about the Suez Canal and the Panama Canal.
Who is the highest run scorer in cricket?
Who is the highest wicket taker in cricket?
Which is the best cricket team in the world across all formats?
tips: Most questions come from your form, so prepare everything you write, especially hobbies and games.
Do not take pressure and stay confident.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Faisalabad centre
experiences.summary: A Colonel took a short interview. He asked the candidate to introduce himself and what he would do if he was not recommended. He then asked which game he plays and about the bad effects of video games and mobile phones. After that he let him go.
asked: Introduce yourself.
If we do not recommend you, what will you do?
Which game do you play?
What are the negative effects of video games?
What are the negative effects of mobile phones?
tips: Do not lose your confidence.
Greet with salam when you enter and leave, and say thank you.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Captain-only interview
experiences.summary: Only a Captain took the whole interview, in a friendly way. He asked for an introduction, some geography and science GK, and about games and hobbies. He also asked why the candidate wants to join the Army. The friendly, smiling talk ended with 'Well done, you may go'.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Where is Nigeria and why is it famous?
Where is Egypt and why is it famous?
How many bones are there in the adult human body?
What are your games and hobbies?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
tips: Talk naturally and smile; treat it as a friendly conversation.
Work hard, pray and trust in Allah.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Peshawar centre (name and maps)
experiences.summary: About 55 candidates came that day and he was second last, so he waited a long time. A Colonel and a psychologist Major took the interview. They asked the meaning of his name, his marks, why he wants to join the Army, and some map and Army questions. The interview lasted only a few minutes, and only 8 or 9 out of 55 were selected.
asked: What is the meaning of your name?
What were your matric and FSc marks?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Where are Asia and Europe on the map?
Where are Russia and Greenland on the world map?
What is the budget of the Pakistan Army?
What are the ranks of non-commissioned officers in the Army?
tips: Be ready for a long wait; stay fresh and calm.
Speak loudly and clearly, and keep your hands and feet still.
Know Army ranks and have a rough idea of the defence budget.
Most candidates fail because they lose confidence, not because of hard questions.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Peshawar centre (female candidate)
experiences.summary: Her essays were on Iqbal's Shaheen and the impact of social media on moral values. She stood by the chair until told to sit. The officer asked about her surname, asked her to describe Islamophobia, and asked map questions about Moscow. He also asked her height in inches, her district and where she was doing her BS.
asked: What does your surname mean? Is it your caste?
Describe Islamophobia.
Where is Moscow, and in which continent is it?
What is your height in inches?
Which is your district?
Where are you doing your BS?
tips: Know your height in inches and other personal details exactly.
Learn the map locations of major world capitals.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • GK and science questions
experiences.summary: After a self-introduction, the interviewer moved to general knowledge, history, science and simple maths. Questions covered Pakistan's provinces, cities and neighbours, World War 2, democracy and the Two Nation Theory. He was also asked intermediate science, like Mendel's laws, and a train speed problem.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What is democracy?
Explain World War 2.
Where is gold found in Pakistan?
What are Mendel's laws?
What is the difference between organic and inorganic compounds?
Name four cities of Sindh.
How many provinces does Pakistan have? Name them.
Name the neighbouring countries of Pakistan.
A train moving at 60 km/h takes 120 seconds to pass through a tunnel. How long is the tunnel? (ignore the train's length)
What is the Two Nation Theory?
tips: Revise your intermediate science subjects, because basic concept questions are asked.
Practise simple speed, time and distance sums in your head.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Bio data form questions
experiences.summary: After the physical test, candidates filled a bio data form for the interview. The form asked about the merits and demerits of himself, his parents, his best friend and his siblings. It also asked what his parents taught him, how he reacts to criticism and his biggest problem as a teenager. These answers are later used by the interviewers.
asked: What are your merits and demerits?
What are the good and bad qualities of your parents, best friend and siblings?
What have your parents taught you?
How do you respond when someone criticises you?
What was your biggest problem as a teenager?
tips: Think about honest answers on your own and your family's strengths and weaknesses before filling the form.
Keep your interview answers the same as what you wrote in the form.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Short interview (called by wrong name)
experiences.summary: A Colonel and a psychologist took the interview. The Colonel called him by a similar-sounding wrong name and he answered without noticing, which annoyed the Colonel a little. He calmly explained the mix-up. The psychologist said his Urdu was weak; they spoke Urdu and he answered confidently in English. The interview lasted about 2 minutes.
asked: What is your full name?
Your Urdu is very weak. Why?
Where did you complete your FSc?
tips: Listen carefully; if you did not hear clearly, politely ask them to repeat.
If you make a mistake, stay calm and explain briefly.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Multan centre
experiences.summary: His essays were on limited internet access for students (English) and unity of the Muslim Ummah (Urdu). He stood near the chair, said salam and sat when asked. A Captain asked him to introduce himself and asked only questions from his bio data form, with no GK. Out of 40 candidates, 18 passed.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Questions from your bio data form
tips: Know everything you wrote in your bio data form.
Still prepare GK, because other candidates were asked GK questions.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Shortest interview
experiences.summary: His interview was the shortest in a batch of about 45 boys. He was asked what foreign policy is and a simple speed-distance sum. The panel also asked about his marks and what he would do if not selected. He calmly said he still had more chances to try.
asked: What is foreign policy?
If a train moves at 33 km per hour, how far will it go in 3 hours?
What are your marks?
What will you do if you are not selected?
tips: Be ready for quick mental maths.
Have a calm, positive answer for 'what if you are not selected'.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Peshawar centre (one 'sorry')
experiences.summary: He wrote an English and an Urdu essay before the interview. The Colonel asked how many times he had applied, his name and what he is doing these days. When asked how Pakistan can improve relations with Afghanistan, he said sorry. He was still recommended.
asked: How many times have you applied to the armed forces?
What are you doing these days?
How can Pakistan improve relations with Afghanistan?
tips: One 'sorry' does not mean rejection; stay polite and confident.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Peshawar centre
experiences.summary: His English essay was 'Honesty is the best policy' and his Urdu essay was 'My favourite personality'. He was asked how Pakistan can improve its relations with Iran and his height in inches. The other questions came from what he filled in his form.
asked: How can Pakistan improve its relationship with Iran?
What is your height in inches?
Questions from your form
tips: Know your exact height, weight and other personal details.
Remember everything you wrote in your form.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Peshawar centre (3-minute interview)
experiences.summary: He wrote two essays, one in English and one in Urdu. The interview lasted only about 3 minutes. He was asked where Mangla Dam is and two questions about the map of Pakistan. Only 7 out of 26 candidates in his group were recommended.
asked: Where is Mangla Dam?
Point out places on the map of Pakistan.
tips: Study the map of Pakistan: dams, rivers and important places.
The interview can be very short, so make a good first impression.

experiences.title: PN Cadet (Navy) • Psychologist interview
experiences.summary: After the Navy written test he had a short interview with a psychologist, fully in English. He asked permission, gave salam clearly and sat when told. She asked him to introduce himself, about his father's rank and unit, and why he wants to join the Navy. He felt she was mainly checking speaking skill and confidence.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What is your father's rank and unit?
Why do you want to join the Pak Navy?
tips: Speak in English with confidence.
Your matric and FSc marks also count in the final list, along with test and interview.

answers.What is the meaning of your name?: Find out the real meaning of your name before the interview and say it in one short line. If it is linked to a famous person or quality, you may mention that.
answers.How do you pronounce your name?: Say your full name slowly and clearly, the same way it is written in your documents.
answers.What are you doing these days?: Tell the truth: your current studies or work, plus how you are preparing for the Army (fitness, reading, GK). Show that you are using your time well.

answers.Why do you want to join the Pakistan Arm: Give a personal, honest reason like serving the country, a life of discipline and leadership, or inspiration from a real person you know. Avoid only saying 'for the uniform' or 'for the salary'.

answers.How do you respond when someone criticis: Say you listen calmly, think about whether it is right, and use it to improve. Give a small real example if you can.
answers.What was your biggest problem as a teena: Mention a real, normal problem (like time management, shyness or a study difficulty) and explain how you handled it and what you learned.
answers.You were a house prefect. Tell me about: Explain what duties you had, one problem you solved, and how you treated the people under you. Only claim roles you really had.
answers.What big thing do you want to do for you: Give a simple, realistic aim, like being a good officer who serves with honesty, supports your family and helps people of your area. Avoid big empty promises.
answers.What is your height in inches?: Know your exact height and weight in both feet-inches and centimetres before the interview, and answer quickly.
answers.Do you tell lies?: Answer honestly and calmly. You can admit you are human, but say you value truth and try your best to always be honest.
answers.Can you explain what you wrote in your b: Read your form copy again before the interview. Every answer you give should match what you wrote there.
answers.How do you think your interview went?: Answer briefly and politely, for example that you tried your best and learned something. Do not argue or sound overconfident.

answers.Do you have siblings? What are their nam: Give each sibling's name, age order and what they study or do in one short line each.
answers.What have your parents taught you?: Mention 2-3 real values like honesty, respect and hard work, with a small example from your life.

answers.Do you have any relative serving in the: Answer truthfully. If yes, say who and their relation to you; if no, simply say no.
answers.Your grades are low. Why?: Accept it honestly and do not blame your school, teachers or anyone else. Say what caused it and what you are doing now to improve.
answers.You got good marks in FSc pre-medical, s: Explain honestly that the Army is your real interest and first choice. Do not speak badly of other careers.
answers.How many times have you applied to the a: Tell the exact number truthfully. If you applied many times, show it as determination and say what you improved each time.
answers.Why were you not recommended in your las: Be honest about what went wrong (for example nervousness or weak GK) and clearly say what you have improved since then.
answers.Why did you change your test centre?: Give the real reason in one line, such as moving for studies or family. Keep it simple and truthful.

Before the interview: Clearing the written test is only the first step; many candidates fail the interview, so start preparing for it right after the test.
Fill the bio data form honestly and remember every answer, because the officers ask questions from it.
Prepare a clear one-minute self-introduction, the meaning of your name, and a real reason for joining the Army.
Know your hobbies, sports and your own study subjects in detail.
Know your exact personal details, including your height in inches and your marks.
Learn current office holders (President, PM, Chief Ministers, Governors, Chairman Senate, NA Speaker), world capitals and currencies.
Practise reading the map of Pakistan and the world map: continents, major countries, dams and rivers.
Revise basic GK: Pakistan's history, constitutions, Pakistan-India wars, Army ranks, military awards and Islamic history.
Follow current news, including your home area and big sports events.
Dress formally: light full-sleeve shirt with sleeves down, dark dress pants, formal lace-up shoes and neat hair; no jeans or loafers. Expensive clothes are not needed.
Take your original documents, copies of certificates and CNIC/B-form, and extra photos to the selection centre.
Expect a long wait on interview day; stay fresh, calm and trust Allah.
In the room: Knock, ask 'May I come in, sir?', and greet both officers with salam.
Stand beside the chair and sit only when told; say thank you.
Sit straight, do not cross your legs or lock your hands, and keep your hands and feet still.
Keep eye contact and a natural smile throughout.
Speak in a clear, loud voice; most of the interview is usually in English.
The board is usually a Colonel or Lt Col with a psychologist Major or a Captain; respect all of them equally.
The interview is short (often 2-10 minutes), so your first impression matters a lot.
When leaving, stand up, thank the panel, say salam and walk out calmly.
Answering: Confidence and the way you speak matter more than knowing every answer.
If you do not know an answer, politely say 'Sorry sir, I don't know' instead of guessing; one sorry is not rejection, but avoid many.
Answer personal and honesty questions truthfully and calmly.
Be honest about weak marks or past failures, and never blame your school, college or others.
Listen carefully; if you did not hear clearly, politely ask the officer to repeat.
If you are weak in one area, say so honestly and offer your strong subject.
Be ready for quick mental maths and estimation questions, like distance, time or the size of a table.
Be ready to speak for 2 minutes on a random topic.
Be ready for the interview to switch suddenly from Urdu to English.
Show confidence but do not be overconfident or argue.
Essay: You write one English and one Urdu essay before the interview, worth about 20 marks in total; practise both.
Use a simple structure: short introduction, main points, and a clear conclusion.
On debate topics, give both sides first and then your own balanced opinion.
Add one famous quote or a simple fact to make the essay stronger.
Learn a few good words with their meanings and use them correctly.
Prepare personal topics like your happiest moment, saddest moment and aim in life, and link the lesson to joining the Army.
Manage your time so you finish both essays.
